Maria Chen: FYI - p99 host-side latency jumped ~45ms after the kernel-selection roll from last night. Root looks like extra CPU in tokenization/parse path and more KV-cache misses.
AJ: ugh. saw similar in infra dashboards, which service?
Maria Chen: serving-prod, ingress path -> host-preproc. Mostly streaming/chat routes. spike correlates with higher small-request rate (avg tokens 12).
Kevin Patel: do we have flamegraphs from the canary? can you paste the perf link?
Maria Chen: uploaded a short perf capture: https://perf.internal/reports/2345689012 - main hotspot is host_tokenizer::tokenize_batch and parse::stream_framing::coalesce
perf-bot: new profile available: /profiles/2345689012/summary (hot functions: host_tokenizer::tokenize, request_parser::deserialize, kvcache::lookup)
Nina Gomez: interesting that kernel selection could affect this - how?
Maria Chen: theory: kernel change altered batch sizing (smaller micro-batches), which increases per-request tokenization overhead and causes KV cache set churn because more distinct prefixes are loaded then evicted. Also noticed more short writes on gRPC -> more syscalls.
AJ: can you paste the minimal repro command? I want to run locally with a perf marker.
Maria Chen: repro using loadgen: 
```
loadgen --target serving-prod:443 --route /chat.stream --qps 1200 --tokens 8-20 --concurrency 400 --run 60s --tag regression-2345
```
Also repro with local canary build of runtime v0.87.2+kernopt.
Kevin Patel: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) bump batching window from 3ms->6ms for small-token routes, 2) guard tokenization path with a tokenizer pool to reuse allocations, 3) tune KV cache shard TTL or increase capacity temporarily.
Nina Gomez: +1 on tokenizer pool, we have a simple allocator in eng-runtime that was removed in kernel refactor. Reintroduce and measure.
Maria Chen: experimented with naive tokenizer pool patch - reduced tokenize CPU by ~28% on local. Patch: 
```
// pseudo
struct TokenizerPool { Vec<Tokenizer> free; Mutex m; }
impl TokenizerPool { fn get(&self) -> Tokenizer { ... } fn put(&self,t){...} }
```

prod perf diff after small pool patch (canary): p50 -3ms, p95 -9ms, p99 -31ms.
AJ: nice. what about gRPC write aggregation? more small writev calls increase syscall overhead. can we coalesce outgoing chunks in ingress proxy?
Kevin Patel: we have an ingress patch that batches streaming writes for <64byte chunks. try enabling for canary. config flag: `ingress.coalesce_small_chunks=true`
Maria Chen: enabled it, local shows syscall writev down 40%. Combined with tokenizer pool, p99 drops ~55ms.
Nina Gomez: excellent. we should still fix root cause for KV churn - maybe kernel selection should be aware of small-token-heavy workloads and choose a different kernel profile that favors larger batch assembly.
Maria Chen: agree. plan: revert kernel-selection heuristic change in canary -> add workload-tagging in kernel selector to prefer batching-for-short-requests, reintroduce tokenizer pool, enable ingress coalescing flag, and increase kvcache small-shard capacity for 24h as safety.
AJ: rollout plan?
Maria Chen: 1) push tokenizer-pool+coalesce flags to canary (in 15m) 2) if stable for 30m, promote to 10% traffic 3) revert kernel heuristic in separate PR and do A/B test 4) monitor p99/token costs and kvcache missrate metrics.

perf-bot: alert suppressed for serving-prod host-preproc for 20m (ack by Maria Chen)
Kevin Patel: tracking issue? put checklist in eng-runtime board and assign me + nina + maria.
Maria Chen: created issue: https://issues.internal/ENG-rt/4591 - added checklist and tentative schedule. tagging @Kevin @Nina for review. :thumbsup:
AJ: thanks team. if canary looks good i'll coordinate rollback window and followups.
Nina Gomez: postmortem note: include kernel-selection unit tests that simulate short-token micro-bursts, and add regression perf tests for kvcache missrate under high small-request qps.
Maria Chen: adding that to the issue. closing the thread for now, will update after 10% rollout.
